chunks: He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Makki, who reported from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who reported from his father, who reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, who reported from Sharik, from Abi Rabi’ah al-Iyadi — and we saw Ma’mar listening from him — from Ibn Buridah, from his father, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Indeed, Allah has commanded me to love four of my companions, and has informed me that He loves them." We said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? And there is none among us who does not wish to be among them." So he, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Behold! Indeed Ali is among them" — he repeated it three times — "and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farsi."

key_terms.أَصْحَابِي: my companions: The Prophet's close followers (ashab), here specifically four individuals
key_terms.أَمَرَنِي: commanded me: Divine imperative indicating Allah's direct order to the Prophet regarding these four companions
key_terms.بِحُبِّ: to love: Divinely mandated spiritual and emotional attachment (hubb)
key_terms.يُحِبُّهُمْ: He loves them: Allah's love (mahabbah) for these four, affirming their elevated station

ai.seo_question: Which four companions did Allah command the Prophet Muhammad to love?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.a.) declared that Allah commanded him to love four specific companions: Ali (emphasized three times), al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farsi. This hadith is transmitted through a notable Sunni chain including Ahmad ibn Hanbal, highlighting cross-sectarian recognition.
